Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.

1. Learned A.G.A. has informed that notice to the informant has been served on 12.7.2024.
2.

Heard Sri Rajesh Yadav, learned counsel for the applicant as well as Sri R.P. Patel, learned A.G.A.
for the State and perused the record.
3. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No.154 of 2024, under Sections 363, 366, 376 I.P.C. and 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station- Paniyara, District- Maharajganj, during the pendency of trial.

sentences.text:
PROSECUTION STORY:
4. The applicant is stated to have enticed away the minor daughter of the informant on 1.5.2024 at about 03:00 a.m.
When the informant went to report the matter, the family members of the applicant are stated to have threatened her and hurled abuses on her.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF APPLICANT:
5. The applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
He has nothing to do with the said offence.
6. The FIR is delayed by about two days and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.

7. Although the applicant is named in the FIR, the victim has categorically denied being enticed away by the applicant in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
8.

As per the school certificate of Class-5th, the date of birth of the victim is stated to be 5.10.2007,
as such her age comes out to be 16 years, 04 months and 28 days.
Even the said certificate is not admissible in evidence in the light of Section 94 of Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act.

entities.text: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 9. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.

The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
10.
There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 17.5.2024 and is ready to cooperate with trial.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF STATE/OPPOSITE PARTY 11.
The bail application has been opposed but the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicant could not be disputed.

CONCLUSION:
12.

In the case of P. Yuvaprakash vs State Rep. by Inspector of Police, AIR 2023 SC 3525 the Supreme Court has observed that in the absence of records relating to the birth of the victim, no other documents except the Matriculation or equivalent certificate from the concerned examination board or certificate by a corporation, municipal authority or a Panchayat can be relied upon to ascertain the age of the victim.

entities.text: P. Yuvaprakash vs State Rep. by Inspector of Police, AIR 2023 SC 3525
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 13. The well-known principle of "Presumption of Innocence Unless Proven Guilty," gives rise to the concept of bail as a rule and imprisonment as an exception.

sentences.text: A person's right to life and liberty, guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because the person is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is established beyond a reasonable doubt.

Article 21 of the Indian Constitution states that no one's life or personal liberty may be taken away unless the procedure established by law is followed, and the procedure must be just and reasonable.
The said principle has been recapitulated by the Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 15. Reiterating the aforesaid view the Supreme Court in the case of Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement 2024 INSC 595 has again emphasised that the very well-settled principle of law that bail is not to be withheld as a punishment is not to be forgotten.

entities.text: Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement 2024 INSC 595
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is high time that the Courts should recognize the principle that ?bail is a rule and jail is an exception?.
16. Learned AGA could not bring forth any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.
17. It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.

No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned AGA.

18. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, taking into consideration that FIR is delayed by about two days and the victim has not named the applicant in her statement recorded U/s 164 Cr.P.C. coupled with the fact that applicant has no criminal antecedent to his credit, and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

19. Let the applicant- Golu Sahani Alias Abhishek involved in aforementioned case crime number be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.

(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C. If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
20. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the court concerned before the bonds are accepted.
